surface: gymlogger-x microsite: /apps/gymlogger-x/ (Persuade) + /apps/gymlogger-x/privacy/, /apps/gymlogger-x/support/ and the alternatives pages that target it: /alternatives/strong-workout-app/, /alternatives/fitbod/, /alternatives/jefit/ (Read variants)

dossier.mechanism: GymLogger X makes the Apple Watch the actual training log. Sets, reps, RPE and rest are entered on the wrist while the phone stays in the locker. A published rule then reads that log and raises a plateau flag: Epley e1RM fails to clear a threshold set by your own 90-day rate of gain (clamped 0.05–1% per session) across four non-deload sessions, while volume holds within 3%. The flag lists possible causes and leaves the programming call to you. Free at the core, $39.99 to own Pro outright, no account.
dossier.audienceScene: A lifter mid-session in a commercial or garage gym: phone in a locker or gym bag, Apple Watch on the wrist, 90–180 s of rest between sets under flat overhead LED/fluorescent light. The page itself is mostly read on that phone, after searching 'Strong app alternative' or 'Apple Watch strength training app': on the bench between sets, on the commute, or on the sofa that evening.
dossier.culturalHome: Barbell culture: powerlifting meets (three referee lights, fault cards, attempt cards, Wilks/DOTS on the results sheet), RPE and %1RM charts taped to rack uprights, the paper training log in shorthand (80×6 @8), the community program spreadsheets (5/3/1, nSuns, GZCL, Sheiko, all built around a Training Max and a deload week, as the studio's own 5/3/1 journal post spells out), evidence-based lifting that argues from studies, and the changing room where the phone gets left.
dossier.mustProve: In the first viewport: (1) the log lives on the wrist, not the phone; (2) the plateau rule is published and checkable, so show the rule (or run it), not a claim about it; (3) it is free to start and $39.99 once for everything, with no account, and the working App Store badge (plus the QR on desktop) is within reach.
dossier.categoryDefault: Dark gym-app landing: near-black ground, neon green or electric-orange accent, an angled iPhone + Watch render or a muscular stock photo, 'Train smarter. Lift stronger.' (the app's own hero.secondary is exactly this line), three icon feature cards, a pricing table with a 'Most popular' ribbon, and star-rated testimonials.
dossier.predictableOpposite: Soft wellness minimalism: pale pastel ground, rounded friendly sans, one floating phone, airy 'mindful movement' copy. Calm but indistinguishable from a habit or meditation app, and close to the retired Paper & Ink template.
dossier.literalReading: 'GymLogger' read literally is the paper logbook: a ruled notebook with handwritten sets. Candidate 3 (the lifter's notebook in shorthand) is the one candidate allowed to use it. It pictures what the wrist replaces, not the wrist.

transparency.yml: 0 third-party SDKs, 0 tracking domains, no account, no network calls for core logging (optional iCloud only), analytics none, sole permission 'Apple Watch connectivity'. 1,500+ exercises ship inside the app.

testimonials.yml: 5 real quotes. K.D. (App Store), P.O. (Reddit, on the import function), P.S. (Reddit), R.O. (App Store), M. (App Store, French, with English translation). Quotes may be used; their star fields must not be shown.

Developer's own reasoning (journal 'the-strength-logger-no-one-asked-for'): 'In the gym, your phone is in a locker, in a bag, on a bench, somewhere not on your body. Your watch is on your body.' Also: plateau detection 'informs without lecturing'; about 30% of paid users pick lifetime. The LiftLog post adds: 'live on Apple Watch and want speed → GymLogger X; live on iPhone and want polish → LiftLog'. So the sibling LiftLog owns polish and equipment, and GymLogger X owns the wrist, speed and the published rule.

App look: the icon is a navy #0f2f4a dumbbell bent into a U with a teal #3f8a8a check, on off-white. Dark navy UI screens: 1.png live Push Day with set chips, a green CURRENT card and an orange 00:47 rest ring; 2.png Progress Overview with a Plateau Detection list in orange 'Monitoring' and Training Balance push/pull 76:24; coach-hero.png coach profile. Light screens: 3.png PRs/Top 1RM; 4.png Push Day template with a superset; 5.png Training home; 6.png muscle-balance heatmap. SF Pro, with system green, blue and orange.

Asset gaps: no Apple Watch screenshot exists even though the Watch is the primary surface. All six screenshot alt texts describe screens other than the files (4.png's alt claims a Watch set screen; it is an iPhone template editor; 2.png's alt claims the Program Creator; it is the Progress overview).

Read surfaces: privacy page (seo block present; overview, data_collection, data_storage, third_parties, sensitive_data, children, changes), support page (seo present), and the Strong, Fitbod and Jefit alternatives pages (card-grid comparisons + FAQPage). The Hevy, Caliber and Heavyset pages target LiftLog. The Strong page's lead wrongly calls GymLogger X a 'native Mac-and-iPhone alternative'. Founder signal prose hard-codes '19 privacy-first apps', which must become a computed count. /apps/gymlogger-x/coaches/ also exists outside this surface list.

candidates.name: Three White Lights (powerlifting meet judging)
candidates.why: Every lifter has watched a meet clip end on the light board. It carries the mechanism exactly: independent calls (e1RM vs your own bar, volume held within 3%, a fatigue or six-session confirmation) must agree before a red 'no lift' verdict lights. The red light comes with a card naming the cause (frequency, recovery, exercise selection, technique), and the lifter, not the referee, chooses the next attempt. The three attempts also give an honest pricing form.

candidates.name: The rack chart (RPE / %1RM table)
candidates.why: The RTS RPE chart and Epley %1RM tables are taped to rack uprights and known cell by cell. They carry the mechanism because the app's maths is that chart (e1RM = weight × (1 + reps/30), RPE first-class), and the plateau rule reads as the chart's own footnote. A table glanced at between sets is exactly what now lives on the wrist.

candidates.name: The lifter's notebook in shorthand
candidates.why: This was the universal ritual before apps (Bench 80×6 @8, deloads bracketed, PRs circled) and it is the literal reading of 'Logger', so it is the rut's one allowed use. It carries the mechanism only weakly: the margin can annotate the plateau rule, but the page pictures the phone-free past rather than the wrist.

candidates.name: The program spreadsheet
candidates.why: Reddit-era lifters ran their training from passed-around 5/3/1, nSuns, GZCL and Sheiko sheets. These have yellow input cells for a Training Max, formulas rounding to 2.5 kg, week tabs, a deload tab and a formula bar where curious lifters checked the maths. They carry the mechanism because the plateau rule becomes a formula you can read, the prices and break-even become cells that show their working, and the app is the sheet that finally fits on a wrist.

candidates.name: The study write-up (structured abstract)
candidates.why: Lifters who track RPE and e1RM argue from studies (strength-science journals, evidence-based lifting sites). The format carries the mechanism through its sections: the plateau rule becomes Methods (Epley as a numbered equation), who_not_for becomes Limitations, 'no investors' becomes the Conflicts statement, and CSV export becomes Data availability. A published rule is literally a published method.

candidates.name: The wrist play card
candidates.why: This is the forearm call-card from American football: an elastic sleeve with a clear vinyl window over a grid of numbered calls, read between snaps. It is the one cultural object that is literally information worn on the wrist, so it carries watch-first directly (the playbook, here the phone, stays on the sideline). But it belongs to football, not barbell culture, so resonance with lifters is partial.

candidates.name: The locker bank
candidates.why: This is the gym's changing room: powder-coated steel doors with pressed louvre vents, engraved name plates, a cam lock and the key on a coiled wrist band with a tag. It is the scene the developer's whole bet starts from ('your phone is in a locker… your watch is on your body'). It carries the mechanism because the phone is literally shut inside while the band on your wrist carries what you need on the floor, and the page can be that one locker door.

styles.label: Phone in the Locker
styles.lineage: Changing-room locker banks of municipal gyms and Nordic swimming halls. Powder-coated sheet steel (RAL 6033 mint turquoise is almost exactly the icon's check-mark teal), rows of pressed louvre vents at the top and foot of each door, and 8px dark seams between doors. Two-ply engraved laminate plates (navy face cut through to a white core) are screwed on with slotted screws. A pressed-steel card holder takes a slid-in label, and the cam lock's key hangs on a coiled plastic wrist band with a numbered tag. Inside: a hat shelf, a hook, laminated house-rules sheets, and the manufacturer's riveted data plate at the foot.
styles.thesis: The page is one locker door, and the phone is shut inside it. The App Store action hangs on the key's wrist band, the thing you actually carry onto the floor. This refuses the category's floating-phone neon hero by making the product's absence from the first viewport the argument.
styles.scene: A lifter in a gym changing room before a session, under flat cool fluorescent tubes: the phone goes onto the locker shelf, the key band goes onto the wrist. Deep painted steel with light lettering, so the scheme is dark (color-scheme: dark).

specimen.h1: Strength training log for iPhone & Apple Watch.

fixes.text: Re-derive every visitorPath from the world's own reading order, and enforce two rules. (1) Within a surface, no two styles may share the relative order of more than two of {price, screenshots, comparison, privacy record, founder, FAQ}. (2) At least one style per surface must change GROUPING, not just order: for example, FAQ split into the sections it answers, who_for/who_not_for folded into the price, or the privacy record as the opener. World-native examples: tare-b sets Puzzle No. 1 before the Rules and puts price and answers at the back like a book. studio-a, allpaid-c and rightsplit-a open with the record (bin label, statement, label data) before any feature. soon-b prints the fare and stub (price) on the face, first. gymlogger-x-c shows the plateau formula before any offer. xiangqiful-c files each FAQ as a margin question on the entry it concerns. observa-b ends on 'past issues' (release notes) instead of a closing CTA block. The maker/freshness line and the shared footer strip may stay common.

gymlogger-x-a keeps the teal, because RAL 6033 is its icon's check colour. mediakit-b keeps line maps: routing a file is wayfinding, and it is MediaKit's #1. Glaze xiangqiful-a's wall in a station colour no surface drenches in, e.g. grey-violet (~#5E5872), avoiding red/gold. Carry the game and the opponents with platform signage instead: direction boards, platform-number blades and bilingual exit lettering, with no octilinear lines or interchange rings.

Keep it on observa-b and soon-c, where its public-service/US-government lineage is native (a public weather bulletin, a NASA-style press kit). Set gymlogger-x-a's laminated sheets and plates in Karla 400/600 (unused) with tabular figures.

Add one production task to every style: a one-off script in scripts/ (already excluded from the build, so it is not a deploy build step) that commits derivatives. Icons at 64, 128 and 256px (WebP plus a PNG fallback, about 15 KB or less at 128). Screenshots at 400w, 800w and 1200w WebP (about 40, 90 and 160 KB or less). The studio mark as the clean SVG that studio a/b/c already ask for. Front matter keeps the original paths; one include maps them to the derivatives and emits width/height, srcset/sizes, loading=lazy and decoding=async (eager plus fetchpriority=high only for a single hero image).

Make it a global contract: html { scroll-padding-top: var(--sticky-top); scroll-padding-bottom: var(--sticky-bottom) }, so focus and anchors never land under a bar. Allow one sticky element per edge, pad the bottom bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and on viewports shorter than 600px hide the top strip while the bottom bar is showing.

Open the door on whichever happens first: IntersectionObserver at 35%, :focus-within on the interior, :target or hash navigation, or beforeprint. Start the safety net 2.5s after the section first intersects, not after page load. Once open, the door is aria-hidden with pointer-events:none. Give the section overflow: clip so the swing can't cause horizontal scroll.

Keep Big Shoulders on taskful-day-a (marquee tiles) and Public Sans on observa-b and soon-c. Move gymlogger-x-a to Teko 700 (a squared athletic condensed suited to cut vinyl, 7 KB) and Ubuntu Sans 400/600 (16 to 17 KB) with tabular figures for kg and prices.

Before build, rewrite the quick_answer clause to match plateau_disclosure, e.g. 'flags a plateau when estimated 1RM stops clearing your own improvement threshold across your last four non-deload sessions while volume holds (it needs 8+ sessions on the lift and 12 weeks of history)'. The AEO answer and the demo must state one rule.

styles.label: Three White Lights
styles.lineage: Powerlifting meet officiating under IPF and national-federation rules. The referee light board shows three round lenses, white = good lift, red = no lift, appearing together once all three referees have pressed. Coloured fault cards are raised beside a red light to name the reason. The lifter or coach hands in an attempt card within a minute to declare the next weight. The Technical Rules book is written in numbered clauses, and the scoring table's results sheet carries Wilks, DOTS and GL points.
styles.thesis: The plateau rule is judged in public like a lift. Three lenses read your sessions, red lights come with a card naming the possible cause, and the next attempt stays yours. This refuses the category's 'AI coach' black box and floating-phone hero with a working judging console.
styles.scene: A lifter at the scorer's table of a local meet, attempt card in hand, under the hall's flat white LED high-bays, with the light board on its stand at the platform edge. Forms and card stock are daylight objects, so the scheme is light; the black housings carry the lenses.

styles.navigation: The black light-board bar carries the wordmark and anchor links (The wrist · The rule · Attempts · Results · Questions), with Privacy and Support set apart at the far right. styles.signatureInteraction: Call the lift. The console runs the published rule's strength-and-volume test on six editable illustrative sessions: Epley e1RM per session, a least-squares trend over the last four against a threshold you set inside the 0.05–1% clamp, volume change against −3%, and a 'fatigue signal' toggle or a six-session run for confirmation. After a 400ms deliberation pause the three lenses switch together, as on a real board: red for each stalled signal, white otherwise. Three reds raise the red cause card ('Plateau flagged … your call'); two reds read 'Monitoring'; three whites read 'Good lift: keep progressing'. It is labelled simplified: the app also needs ≥8 sessions, 12 weeks of history and confidence > 0.4. No-JS: server-rendered example values with the lenses in their computed state and the verdict printed. Reduced motion: no pause; lenses switch instantly.
styles.motionGrammar: Officiating cadence: discrete and decisive. Lenses change state together after one pause, and the cause card drops in 120ms. The sticky strip slides in 200ms. There are no scroll reveals, no parallax and no glow; everything outside the console holds still on paper.

styles.lineage: The program spreadsheets passed around r/weightroom and r/powerlifting in the 2010s: Wendler 5/3/1 calculators, nSuns 5/3/1 LP, GZCL's Jacked & Tan and The Rippler, Candito 6-Week, Sheiko in Excel. They share a dark merged title band, yellow 'enter your Training Max' input cells, percentages rounded to 2.5 kg by formula, AMRAP '+' cells, a deload tab, week tabs along the bottom, conditional-format fills, a README tab, and the formula bar where lifters checked the maths.
styles.thesis: The page is one workbook where every number shows its formula: the plateau test, e1RM, the annual saving, the lifetime break-even. This refuses the category's 'trust our AI' copy and turns the lifter's own habit of checking the sheet into the proof.
styles.scene: Sunday evening at the kitchen table, laptop open on the program sheet, planning next week's numbers; the white sheet is the light source, so the scheme is light.

styles.navigation: Sheet tabs: Log · Rule · Program · Price · vs Strong · Questions · README, with Privacy and Support set apart at the right end. They are plain anchor links to named ranges (they work without JS). With JS, the active tab tracks scroll with a teal underline. styles.signatureInteraction: Show the working. Click, tap or focus (Tab) any computed number on the page: e1RM, trend, verdict, $23.88/yr monthly cost, the ~25% saving, the 2.2-year break-even, cost-after-n-years. The cell takes the teal selection outline, the Name Box shows its address, and the formula bar shows its formula. Yellow input cells (kg, reps, threshold) are editable and recalculate the dependent cells and conditional fills live. No-JS: every value is server-rendered, the plateau formula is server-rendered in the formula bar, and a visible 'Formulas' range on the Rule sheet lists each key formula so crawlers get them too. Reduced motion: the selection jumps without its 120ms slide, and recalculated cells do not flash.
styles.motionGrammar: Spreadsheet-instant: no easing theatre. The selection outline moves in 120ms, recalculated cells flash a single yellow fill fading over 300ms, conditional fills switch instantly, and the sheet-tab underline slides in 150ms. Nothing scrolls itself and nothing reveals on scroll.

The reading column is one wide merged cell (A:F) with wrap text: Carlito 18px/1.6, 68ch, no gridlines inside it, gridlines only in the frame. The policy's sections are sheet tabs. Alternatives pages: page.title in the navy band; quick_answer as a note cell; a two-column comparison sheet (GymLogger X | Strong) with a frozen first column; trade-off lists; FAQ rows; the badge in the status bar. Fix the Strong page's 'Mac-and-iPhone' error. Support: a 'Contact' sheet with email, response time and a what-to-include checklist as rows.
styles.assetsNeeded: None new: the grid, formula bar and tabs are HTML/CSS, and the badge, QR and screenshots exist. Shared production task: real Apple Watch screenshots and corrected alt text for all six screenshots.
styles.risk: A spreadsheet reads as work, not desire, so Persuade could stall at 'it looks like Excel'. The costume line is thin: use the lifting-sheet grammar (merged bands, yellow inputs, tabs, formula bar) and never Office chrome (no ribbon, no menus, no file name). Grids are cramped at 390px, so only columns A–C are shown and the comparison scrolls inside its range. Carlito is plain at display size, so the navy band and scale must carry the headline. It has the most JS of the three (still small vanilla).
styles.memoryTest: The whole page was a lifting spreadsheet. I tapped the $39.99 and the formula bar showed the break-even maths, and the plateau rule was literally a formula I could poke with my own numbers.

canon: Dark gym-app landing played straight: near-black ground, neon-green accent, angled iPhone + Apple Watch renders, 'Train smarter. Lift stronger.' headline, three icon feature cards, a pricing table with a 'Most popular' ribbon, a star-rated testimonial carousel.
notes: The roll ran degraded (roll service offline, no catalog challengers, no quality-bar boards). Key ae47b3c0 dealt candidate 7 (Style A, THE ROLL). Re-roll 1 dealt candidate 4 (Style C, SECOND ROLL), which was distinct, so no further re-roll was needed. Neither is #1, so Style B is the top-ranked candidate (IMPECCABLE’S PICK). The candidate list and ranking were fixed before the dice were cast. The three styles differ in world (place/object, competition ritual, document grid), topology (one tall door with a swing reveal; a console-led page of forms and numbered clauses; a frozen-pane workbook with tabs and a formula bar) and lighting (dark teal drench; light blue card stock with black housings; restrained white screen). All faces were verified on Fontsource, with latin woff2 sizes measured: Big Shoulders Display 800 14.6 KB, Public Sans 14.6 KB/weight, Chivo 14–15 KB/weight, Chivo Mono 500 12 KB, Carlito 30–31 KB/weight, Fragment Mono 25 KB. None repeats a sibling microsite's faces or worlds as proposed so far. GymLogger X deliberately avoids gym-equipment material (plates, knurling, chalk) so it does not converge on sister app LiftLog. Content flags for the build: (1) no Apple Watch screenshot exists, although the Watch is the primary surface; (2) all six screenshot alts describe the wrong screens; (3) the founder signal hard-codes '19' apps and should be computed; (4) /alternatives/strong-workout-app/ wrongly says 'Mac-and-iPhone'; (5) /apps/gymlogger-x/coaches/ exists and should wear the winning world too, though it is not in this surface list; (6) hero.secondary 'Train smarter. Lift stronger.' is the category cliché, so none of the styles headlines with it; (7) the Hevy, Caliber and Heavyset alternatives pages target LiftLog and wear LiftLog's world, even though they appear in GymLogger X's alternatives_to links.

pageFixes.issue: Below the hero, the three styles of each surface follow one section order with new labels. appmeta-a ≡ appmeta-b, gymlogger-x-a ≡ -b ≡ -c, rightsplit-b ≡ -c, shogiful-b ≡ -c, wanderwiki-a ≡ -b (-c swaps two blocks) and pawza-a ≡ -c. The xiangqiful, earnlock and millrace trios each differ by one swap. Across the 60 microsite styles, one order dominates: hero → quick answer → (quick reference) → how it works → screenshots → features → who_for/who_not_for → price → comparison → privacy → founder/about → (roadmap) → FAQ → further reading → closing. That is one static structure in 60 costumes, which is the thing the owner refused ('do not use the same static structure for each page, build them from scratch'). It also makes the three styles per page skin choices, not page choices.
